added_lemmas.statement:
For the former widening longitudinal density
\[
w_T(x)=\frac{15}{16T}\left(1-\frac{x^2}{T^2}\right)^2\mathbf 1\{|x|\le T\},
\]
assume \(\alpha_n(3T+2\varepsilon)\le1\).  Then
\[
\max_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}G_n(r)
\ge \frac{25T}{128}+\frac{15\varepsilon}{256}.
\]
In particular, for the former schedules \(T_n=2^{\lfloor(\log_2n)/12\rfloor}\) and \(\varepsilon_n=T_n^{-1}\), the left-hand side tends to infinity.  Consequently no finite \(\mathfrak L^\dagger\) and no sequence \(e_n\to0\) can satisfy \(\max_rG_n(r)\le\mathfrak L^\dagger+e_n\) along those schedules.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(\vartheta(t)=(c^\dagger)^\top t\).  The positivity premise and \(\mathrm{prop:unequal\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}exact\text{-}primitives}\) make every \(p_{n,x,h}^\dagger\) a probability distribution, hence make the displayed mixture a genuine prior.  Conditional on \((X^\dagger,H^\dagger)=(x,h)\), the labeled response types are independent with common law \(p_{n,x,h}^\dagger\).  Indeed, for a labeled type sequence with count vector \(m\), multiplication of its multinomial-count probability by the reciprocal orbit size gives
\[
\left\{\frac{n!}{\prod_tm_t!}\prod_t
 (p_{n,x,h,t}^\dagger)^{m_t}\right\}
\left\{\frac{\prod_tm_t!}{n!}\right\}
=\prod_{i=1}^np_{n,x,h,t_i}^\dagger. \tag{1}
\]
This calculation also keeps the target equal to the realized finite-population contrast
\(n^{-1}\sum_i\vartheta(t_i)\); it does not replace that target by a prior mean.

The exact-primitives proposition gives the positive-measure equalities
\[
\sum_t\lambda_{v,t}^+\vartheta(t)^2=\frac58,
\qquad
\sum_t\lambda_{d,t}^+\vartheta(t)^2=\frac3{16}.
\]
Complementing a type changes \(\vartheta(t)\) to \(-\vartheta(t)\), by the zero-sum contrast assumption, and the displayed negative measures are the complements of the positive ones.  Hence
\[
\sum_t\lambda_{v,t}^-\vartheta(t)^2=\frac58,
\qquad
\sum_t\lambda_{d,t}^-\vartheta(t)^2=\frac3{16}. \tag{2}
\]
The central types \(000\) and \(111\) have zero score.  Substitution in the definition of \(p_{n,x,h}^\dagger\) therefore yields the exact conditional second moment
\[
\mathbb E\{\vartheta(t_i)^2\mid x,h\}
=\alpha_n\left(\frac58|x|+\frac3{16}|h|\right). \tag{3}
\]
Direct integration of the two polynomial densities gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E|X^\dagger|
&=\frac{30}{16T}\int_0^Tx\left(1-\frac{x^2}{T^2}\right)^2dx
=\frac{5T}{16},\\
\mathbb E|H^\dagger|
&=\frac{30}{16\varepsilon}\int_0^\varepsilon h
 \left(1-\frac{h^2}{\varepsilon^2}\right)^2dh
=\frac{5\varepsilon}{16}. \tag{4}
\end{aligned}
\]

Now assign units independently with probabilities
\(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\).  Every component is positive.  Define
\[
Z_i=\frac{c_{A_i}^\dagger\{Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-1/2\}}
 {q_{A_i}^\dagger},
\qquad
\overline\tau_{\mathrm{HT}}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nZ_i.
\]
For every fixed schedule, the zero-sum and \(\ell^1\)-normalization assumptions imply
\[
\mathbb E_AZ_i=\vartheta(t_i),
\qquad
\mathbb E_AZ_i^2
=\sum_{a=1}^3\frac{(c_a^\dagger)^2}{4q_a^\dagger}
=\frac12\sum_{a=1}^3|c_a^\dagger|=1. \tag{5}
\]
Independence across units now gives
\[
\mathbb E_A\!\left[
 \{\overline\tau_{\mathrm{HT}}-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2
 \mid y\right]
=\frac1{n^2}\sum_{i=1}^n\{1-\vartheta(t_i)^2\}. \tag{6}
\]
Average (6) under the genuine prior and use (3)--(4) and
\(\alpha_n=n^{-1/3}\).  The result is
\[
\operatorname{BayesRisk}(\overline\tau_{\mathrm{HT}})
=\frac1n-n^{-4/3}\left(\frac{25T}{128}
 +\frac{15\varepsilon}{256}\right). \tag{7}
\]
The normalization assumptions put every target in \([-1,1]\), so projection of
\(\overline\tau_{\mathrm{HT}}\) onto \([-1,1]\) cannot increase squared error.
Conditional on its allocation count \(r\), the independent design is uniform over labeled assignments having that count.  Posterior square completion in
\(\mathrm{def:exact\text{-}tube\text{-}bayes\text{-}risk}\) says that
\(\mathcal B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger(r)\) is the minimum conditional Bayes risk.  If \(\pi\) is the induced count law, then
\[
B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger
\le\sum_r\pi(r)\mathcal B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger(r)
\le\frac1n-n^{-4/3}\left(\frac{25T}{128}
 +\frac{15\varepsilon}{256}\right). \tag{8}
\]
The first inequality says that a minimum is no larger than a convex average; the second compares the posterior mean with the clipped estimator above.  By the definitions of \(B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger\) and \(G_n\), (8) is equivalent to
\[
\max_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}G_n(r)
=n^{4/3}\left\{\frac1n-B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger\right\}
\ge\frac{25T}{128}+\frac{15\varepsilon}{256}. \tag{9}
\]

For the former schedules, \(T_n\le n^{1/12}\), \(T_n\to\infty\), and
\(\varepsilon_n=T_n^{-1}\).  Hence
\[
\alpha_n(3T_n+2\varepsilon_n)
\le3n^{-1/4}+2n^{-1/3}\longrightarrow0, \tag{10}
\]
so the positivity premise holds eventually.  Applying (9) gives
\[
\max_rG_n(r)\ge\frac{25T_n}{128}+\frac{15}{256T_n}
\longrightarrow\infty. \tag{11}
\]
If a finite \(\mathfrak L^\dagger\) and \(e_n\to0\) obeyed the asserted uniform upper bound, its right-hand side would remain bounded, contradicting (11).  This proves every clause.

added_lemmas.statement:
The default branches in \(\mathrm{def:rational\text{-}airy\text{-}longitudinal\text{-}family}\) are never used.  For every \(k\ge1\), \(\varphi_k^\dagger\) has rational breakpoints and rational coefficients, is supported in \([-T_k^\dagger,T_k^\dagger]\), and satisfies
\[
4\int_{\mathbb R}|(\varphi_k^\dagger)'|^2dx
+\kappa(c^\dagger)\int_{\mathbb R}|x|(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2dx
\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+2^{-k}. \tag{A}
\]
Moreover,
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}\left\{|(\varphi_k^\dagger)'-\phi_{c^\dagger}'|^2
+(1+|x|)|\varphi_k^\dagger-\phi_{c^\dagger}|^2\right\}dx
\longrightarrow0. \tag{B}
\]
Thus \(w_k^\dagger\) is a compactly supported probability density that is piecewise polynomial with rational coefficients, and both \(\int(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2\) and the two energy integrals in (A) are exactly rational numbers.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(\Phi=\phi_{c^\dagger}\) and \(\kappa=\kappa(c^\dagger)=5/8\), the latter equality being supplied by
\(\mathrm{prop:unequal\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}exact\text{-}primitives}\).
By the Airy-ground-state definition,
\[
\|\Phi\|_2=1,
\qquad
4\|\Phi'\|_2^2+\kappa\||x|^{1/2}\Phi\|_2^2
=\Lambda_{c^\dagger}<\infty. \tag{1}
\]
We first prove directly that the enumerated rational splines are dense in the weighted norm \(d_\dagger\).

For an integer \(R\ge1\), let \(\chi_R\) be the even piecewise-linear cutoff equal to one on \([-R,R]\), zero outside \([-R-1,R+1]\), and affine on the two intervening unit intervals.  Dominated convergence and (1) give
\[
\int(1+|x|)|(1-\chi_R)\Phi|^2dx\longrightarrow0,
\qquad
\int|(1-\chi_R)\Phi'|^2dx\longrightarrow0. \tag{2}
\]
Since \(|\chi_R'|\le1\) and its support is contained in
\(\{R\le|x|\le R+1\}\), one also has
\(\int|\chi_R'\Phi|^2\to0\).  The product rule and (2) therefore show
\[
d_\dagger(\chi_R\Phi,\Phi)\longrightarrow0. \tag{3}
\]

Fix \(R\) and put \(S=R+1\) and \(f=\chi_R\Phi\).  Then
\(f\in H_0^1(-S,S)\) is even and its weak derivative \(g=f'\) is odd.
Choose an odd rational step function \(q\), on a finite partition with rational endpoints, so that \(\|q-g\|_{L^2(-S,S)}\) is arbitrarily small.  Such a choice follows by first taking cell averages of \(g\) on a sufficiently fine symmetric rational partition and then approximating the finitely many positive-half cell averages by rationals, extending with opposite signs.  In particular \(\int_{-S}^Sq=0\).  Define
\[
p(x)=\int_{-S}^xq(z)dz\quad(-S\le x\le S),
\qquad p(x)=0\quad(|x|>S).
\]
Then \(p\) is even, continuous, piecewise linear, and has rational breakpoints and rational coefficients; also \(p(\pm S)=0\).  Since
\(f(x)=\int_{-S}^xg(z)dz\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
\|p-f\|_\infty\le(2S)^{1/2}\|q-g\|_2,
\qquad
\|p'-f'\|_2=\|q-g\|_2. \tag{4}
\]
On the fixed compact interval, (4) makes both the weighted \(L^2\) error and the derivative error arbitrarily small.  Combining this fact with (3) proves density of the enumerated rational splines in \(d_\dagger\).

Consequently, for every \(k\), the defining set containing
\(\varphi_k^\dagger\) is nonempty.  Because \(\eta_k\le1/2\) while
\(d_\dagger(0,\Phi)\ge\|\Phi\|_2=1\), its selected element is nonzero, so neither default branch is used.  By construction,
\(d_\dagger(\varphi_k^\dagger,\Phi)\le\eta_k\le2^{-k}\), which proves (B).

For any \(p\) with \(d_\dagger(p,\Phi)\le\eta\le1\), the reverse triangle inequality and Cauchy--Schwarz imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
4\left|\|p'\|_2^2-\|\Phi'\|_2^2\right|
&\le4\eta(2\|\Phi'\|_2+\eta),\\
\kappa\left|\||x|^{1/2}p\|_2^2
-\||x|^{1/2}\Phi\|_2^2\right|
&\le\kappa\eta(2\||x|^{1/2}\Phi\|_2+\eta).
\end{aligned} \tag{5}
\]
The definition of \(\eta_k\), (1), and (5) show that the energy of
\(\varphi_k^\dagger\) differs from \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\) by at most
\(2^{-k}\), proving (A).

Finally, a square of a rational piecewise-linear function is a nonnegative rational piecewise-quadratic function.  Integration of its rational polynomial pieces over rational endpoints is rational, as is integration after multiplication by \(|x|\) once the partition is split at zero.  The nonzero rational normalizing integral therefore makes \(w_k^\dagger\) an exactly represented probability density and proves the final assertions.

added_lemmas.statement:
Assume \(\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+2\varepsilon)\le1\).  Under the corrected permutation-invariant prior \(\nu_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\), every outcome-independent assignment law \(\mathcal D_n\) and every possibly randomized labeled-data estimator have Bayes risk at least
\[
\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}\pi(r)
 \mathcal B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
\ge B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A},
\]
where \(\pi\) is the allocation-count law induced by \(\mathcal D_n\).  Conditional on a fixed allocation count, the posterior mean of the exact finite-population target attains the displayed fixed-count Bayes risk.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The total masses of \(\lambda_v^\pm\), \(\lambda_d^\pm\), and
\(p_0^\dagger\) are respectively three, two, and one.  Therefore the perturbation in
\(p_{n,x,h}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\) has total mass zero.  Every noncentral coordinate is nonnegative, while each central coordinate is bounded below by its
\(p_0^\dagger\)-mass multiplied by
\(1-\alpha_n(3|x|+2|h|)\).  The support restrictions and the stated positivity condition make this last quantity nonnegative.  Thus the corrected construction is a probability law.  It is invariant under common permutations of the \(n\) unit labels, and its target is exactly
\(\tau_{c^\dagger}(m)=n^{-1}\sum_tm_t(c^\dagger)^\top t\) by the exact-primitives proposition.

Fix an assignment vector \(a_0\) with count vector \(r\).  Given a response-count vector \(m\), the prior is uniform over all labeled type sequences in that orbit.  Counting the type-by-arm tables compatible with the observed arm-success vector gives exactly
\(P_m(X^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid r)\) from
\(\mathrm{def:three\text{-}arm\text{-}orbit\text{-}likelihood}\).  Moreover, two labeled outcome vectors having the same arm-success counts are carried into one another by a permutation within the three assigned-arm blocks.  The prior and target are invariant under that permutation.  Hence the posterior law of the target depends on the labeled observations only through \((r,X^{\mathrm{obs}})\).

For squared error, conditional completion of the square gives
\[
\mathbb E\{(d-\tau)^2\mid r,X^{\mathrm{obs}}\}
=\operatorname{Var}(\tau\mid r,X^{\mathrm{obs}})
 +\{d-\mathbb E(\tau\mid r,X^{\mathrm{obs}})\}^2. \tag{1}
\]
This remains true after averaging any estimator randomization.  Thus the posterior mean is optimal, and summing its posterior variance using the exact likelihood gives
\(\mathcal B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)\) by
\(\mathrm{def:exact\text{-}airy\text{-}tube\text{-}bayes\text{-}risk}\).

Now let \(A\sim\mathcal D_n\).  Outcome independence means that conditioning on
\(A=a_0\) does not change the schedule prior.  Any two assignment vectors with the same count vector are related by a common unit permutation, so the preceding minimum conditional Bayes risk is the same for both and equals
\(\mathcal B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)\).  Applying (1) conditionally on every assignment vector and grouping by its count gives the first displayed inequality.  The second is the fact that a convex average is at least its smallest summand.  This proves the claim for arbitrary dependence in \(\mathcal D_n\) and arbitrary labeled, randomized estimators.

added_lemmas.statement:
For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\),
\[
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3},
\qquad
\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c^\dagger)\}
=\Lambda_{c^\dagger},
\]
and
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}
\ge\Lambda_{c^\dagger}>0.
\]
Here \(R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\) uses the fixed independent allocation
\(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\).  No equality between the unrestricted and fixed-design second-order values is asserted.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The exact-primitives proposition proves
\(\kappa(c^\dagger)=5/8\), so the Airy-benchmark definition gives
\[
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A\kappa(c^\dagger)^{2/3}
=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}>0. \tag{1}
\]
The already established theorem \(\mathrm{thm:qstar\text{-}second\text{-}order}\), applied to this fixed three-active-arm contrast, yields
\[
R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c^\dagger)
=\frac1n-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}), \tag{2}
\]
which is equivalent to the displayed limit.  The unrestricted minimax game contains the fixed independent design among its feasible design actions; hence
\(R_n(c^\dagger)\le R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c^\dagger)\).  Subtracting this inequality from \(n^{-1}\), multiplying by the positive number \(n^{4/3}\), and taking lower limits proves the second display from (2).  The one-sided order is essential: neither this comparison nor (2) supplies the reverse inequality for the unrestricted game.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix integers \(n,k\ge1\), rational \(\varepsilon>0\), and rational
\(\delta>0\) such that \(\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+2\varepsilon)\le1\).  A terminating exact algorithm returns rationals \(L_{n,k,\varepsilon,\delta}\) and
\(U_{n,k,\varepsilon,\delta}\) satisfying
\[
L_{n,k,\varepsilon,\delta}
\le B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}
\le U_{n,k,\varepsilon,\delta},
\qquad
U_{n,k,\varepsilon,\delta}-L_{n,k,\varepsilon,\delta}\le\delta.
\]
For the unrestricted causal minimax risk at the same sample size,
\[
L_{n,k,\varepsilon,\delta}
\le R_n(c^\dagger)\le\frac1n,
\]
and therefore
\[
0\le n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}
\le n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-L_{n,k,\varepsilon,\delta}\}.
\]
This is a same-input finite certificate; it makes no cross-sample convergence claim.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The rational Airy approximation lemma makes \(w_k^\dagger\) a finite rational piecewise-polynomial density.  Split its support at its finitely many rational breakpoints and at zero, and split the transverse interval at zero.  On each resulting rectangle, every coordinate of
\(p_{n,x,h}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\) is affine in \((x,h)\) with coefficients in
\(\mathbb Q(\alpha_n)\), while \(w_k^\dagger(x)\rho_\varepsilon(h)\) is a rational polynomial.  Consequently every multinomial prior integrand is a polynomial with coefficients in \(\mathbb Q(\alpha_n)\), and exact integration over rational endpoints gives
\[
\nu_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(m)
\in\mathbb Q(\alpha_n) \tag{1}
\]
for every one of the finitely many \(m\in\mathcal M_{n,3}\).  The positivity condition makes these weights probabilities by the corrected orbit lemma.

The factorial formula for \(P_m(X^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid r)\) and the formula for
\(\tau_{c^\dagger}(m)\) are rational.  Enumerating the finite sets of response counts, allocation counts, success counts, and feasible type-by-arm tables therefore evaluates every posterior numerator, denominator, quotient, and
\(\mathcal B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)\) exactly in the ordered real algebraic field \(\mathbb Q(\alpha_n)\).  The minimum over the finite set
\(\mathcal R_{n,3}\) is consequently the exactly represented element
\(B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\).

The number \(\alpha_n\) is the specified positive isolated root of
\(nX^3-1\).  Arithmetic and sign comparison in its degree-at-most-three ordered field terminate by clearing rational denominators and applying the Euclidean algorithm to the fixed polynomial and the polynomial representing the element being compared.  Starting with any rational interval containing the risk, rational bisection and those terminating sign tests produce an enclosure of width at most \(\delta\).  This proves the existence and termination of the algorithm and the first display.

The corrected orbit Bayes lemma applies to every outcome-independent design and estimator.  A maximum risk is at least its average under the corrected prior, so taking the infimum in \(\mathrm{def:risk\text{-}game}\) gives
\[
R_n(c^\dagger)\ge B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}
\ge L_{n,k,\varepsilon,\delta}. \tag{2}
\]
For the reverse finite bound, use independent allocation
\(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\) and the unprojected estimator
\[
\overline\tau=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
 \frac{c_{A_i}^\dagger(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-1/2)}{q_{A_i}^\dagger}.
\]
For every fixed schedule, the zero-sum and \(\ell^1\)-normalization assumptions give
\[
\mathbb E_A\overline\tau=\tau_{c^\dagger}(y),
\qquad
\mathbb E_A\{\overline\tau-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2
=\frac1{n^2}\sum_{i=1}^n\{1-((c^\dagger)^\top Y_i)^2\}
\le\frac1n. \tag{3}
\]
Every target lies in \([-1,1]\), so clipping \(\overline\tau\) to that interval cannot increase loss and gives an admissible total estimator.  Thus the design and estimator in (3) are feasible in the unrestricted game and prove
\(R_n(c^\dagger)\le n^{-1}\).  Combine this with (2), subtract from
\(n^{-1}\), and multiply by \(n^{4/3}>0\) to obtain the remaining displays.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Use the corrected rational Airy longitudinal family and retain the nonzero transverse response measure. There exist computable sequences of integers \(k_n\uparrow\infty\), positive rationals \(\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\downarrow0\), and nonnegative rational certificate errors \(e_n^{\mathrm{loc}},e_n^{\mathrm{shell}},e_n^{\mathrm{zero}},e_n^{\mathrm{pr}}\to0\), with \[\alpha_n\{3T_{k_n}^\dagger+2\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\}\le1,\] such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), writing \(G_n^{\mathrm A}(r)=G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)\), \[\max_{r\in\mathcal F_n(M_n)}(G_n^{\mathrm A}(r)-\Lambda_{c^\dagger})_+\le e_n^{\mathrm{loc}},\] \[\max_{0\le j\le J_n(M_n)}\ \max_{r\in\mathcal S_{n,j}(M_n)}(G_n^{\mathrm A}(r)-\Lambda_{c^\dagger})_+\le e_n^{\mathrm{shell}},\] and \[\max_{\varnothing\ne A\subsetneq\{1,2,3\}}\ \max_{r\in\mathcal Z_{n,A}}(G_n^{\mathrm A}(r)-\Lambda_{c^\dagger})_+\le e_n^{\mathrm{zero}}.\] The certificates are obtained from the exact finite factorial likelihood and retain the identity \(\tau_{c^\dagger}(m)=n^{-1}\sum_tm_t(c^\dagger)^\top t\) on every stratum. A total finite procedure under the independent allocation \(q^\dagger\) satisfies \[\max_y\mathbb E\{(\widehat\tau_n-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y))^2\}\le n^{-1}-(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_n^{\mathrm{pr}})n^{-4/3}.\] Consequently, with \(e_n=\max(e_n^{\mathrm{loc}},e_n^{\mathrm{shell}},e_n^{\mathrm{zero}},e_n^{\mathrm{pr}})\), \[n^{-1}-(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n)n^{-4/3}\le R_n(c^\dagger)\le n^{-1}-(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_n)n^{-4/3}.\]
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current claim is false for its widening density: the exact obstruction gives a Bayes-deficit lower bound growing as \(25T/128\), contradicting the asserted finite tube-removal limit along \(T_n\to\infty\). The proposed claim narrows from all fixed \((T,\varepsilon)\) coefficient expansions to one certified Airy-spline diagonal, retains the full allocation simplex and the nonzero transverse coordinate, and states the still-required all-count bridge as a result rather than assuming it.

proposed.name: Compact rational Airy longitudinal family
proposed.construction:
Put \(\Phi=\phi_{c^\dagger}\), \(\kappa=\kappa(c^\dagger)=5/8\), and
\[
d_\dagger(f,\Phi)^2
=\int_{\mathbb R}\left\{|f'-\Phi'|^2+(1+|x|)|f-\Phi|^2\right\}dx.
\]
Fix an enumeration by natural-number codes of all pairs \((T,p)\) for which \(T\) is a positive integer and \(p\) is an even, continuous, compactly supported piecewise-linear function supported in \([-T,T]\), with rational breakpoints and rational polynomial coefficients on every piece.  For \(k\ge1\), let
\[
\eta_k=\min\!\left\{2^{-k},
\frac{2^{-k}}{8\|\Phi'\|_2+4+2\kappa\||x|^{1/2}\Phi\|_2+\kappa}\right\}.
\]
Define \((T_k^\dagger,\varphi_k^\dagger)\) to be the first pair in this enumeration satisfying \(d_\dagger(\varphi_k^\dagger,\Phi)\le\eta_k\), using the zero function on \([-1,1]\) only as a default if no such pair exists.  When \(\int(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2>0\), set
\[
w_k^\dagger(x)=\frac{\varphi_k^\dagger(x)^2}
 {\int_{\mathbb R}\varphi_k^\dagger(z)^2dz};
\]
on the unused default branch set \(w_k^\dagger(x)=\mathbf1\{|x|\le1\}/2\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The old density widens with \(T\) and forces a divergent deficit; this construction changes only the longitudinal density and leaves the transverse measure untouched.

proposed.name: Corrected exact rational Airy tube prior
proposed.construction:
For integers \(n,k\ge1\) and rational \(\varepsilon>0\) satisfying
\(\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+2\varepsilon)\le1\), retain
\(p_0^\dagger\), \(\lambda_v^\pm\), \(\lambda_d^\pm\),
\(d^\dagger\), and \(\rho_\varepsilon\) unchanged.  On every sign cell of
\(\operatorname{supp}(w_k^\dagger)\times[-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]\), with either sign chosen at a zero coordinate, put
\[
p_{n,x,h,t}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}
=p_{0,t}^\dagger+\alpha_n\left\{
 |x|\lambda_{v,t}^{\operatorname{sign}(x)}
 +|h|\lambda_{d,t}^{\operatorname{sign}(h)}
 -(3|x|+2|h|)p_{0,t}^\dagger\right\}.
\]
Draw \(X^\dagger\) with density \(w_k^\dagger\), draw \(H^\dagger\) independently with density \(\rho_\varepsilon\), draw

proposed.construction:
On input integers \(n,k\ge1\), positive rationals \(\varepsilon,\delta\), and the finite rational spline record for \(\varphi_k^\dagger\), first verify
\(\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+2\varepsilon)\le1\).  Enumerate the finitely many rational spline cells, the eight response types, all response-count vectors \(m\), all allocation counts \(r\), all arm-success vectors, and all feasible type-by-arm tables.  Integrate each polynomial cell exactly in \(\mathbb Q(\alpha_n)\), evaluate
\(B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\), and refine rational isolating intervals until it returns an enclosure \([L,U]\) with \(U-L\le\delta\).  If supplied with proposed local-face, exterior-shell, zero-face, and primal error certificates, the evaluator checks each finite inequality by the same ordered-field comparisons.  This same-input branch is finite.  It reports a cross-sample threshold only after certificates proving the four error sequences tend to zero have been supplied; it does not infer termination of the diagonal search from same-sample exact arithmetic.

proposed.statement:
Use the corrected rational Airy longitudinal family and retain the nonzero transverse response measure.  There exist computable sequences of integers \(k_n\uparrow\infty\), positive rationals \(\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\downarrow0\), and nonnegative rational certificate errors \(e_n^{\mathrm{loc}},e_n^{\mathrm{shell}},e_n^{\mathrm{zero}},e_n^{\mathrm{pr}}\to0\), with
\[
\alpha_n\{3T_{k_n}^\dagger+2\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\}\le1,
\]
such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), writing \(G_n^{\mathrm A}(r)=G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)\),
\[
\max_{r\in\mathcal F_n(M_n)}(G_n^{\mathrm A}(r)-\Lambda_{c^\dagger})_+
\le e_n^{\mathrm{loc}},
\]
\[
\max_{0\le j\le J_n(M_n)}\ \max_{r\in\mathcal S_{n,j}(M_n)}
(G_n^{\mathrm A}(r)-\Lambda_{c^\dagger})_+
\le e_n^{\mathrm{shell}},
\]
and
\[
\max_{\varnothing\ne A\subsetneq\{1,2,3\}}\ \max_{r\in\mathcal Z_{n,A}}
(G_n^{\mathrm A}(r)-\Lambda_{c^\dagger})_+
\le e_n^{\mathrm{zero}}.
\]
The certificates are obtained from the exact finite factorial likelihood and retain the identity \(\tau_{c^\dagger}(m)=n^{-1}\sum_tm_t(c^\dagger)^\top t\) on every stratum.  A total finite procedure under the independent allocation \(q^\dagger\) satisfies
\[
\max_y\mathbb E\{(\widehat\tau_n-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y))^2\}
\le n^{-1}-(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_n^{\mathrm{pr}})n^{-4/3}.
\]
Consequently, with \(e_n=\max(e_n^{\mathrm{loc}},e_n^{\mathrm{shell}},e_n^{\mathrm{zero}},e_n^{\mathrm{pr}})\),
\[
n^{-1}-(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n)n^{-4/3}
\le R_n(c^\dagger)
\le n^{-1}-(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_n)n^{-4/3}.
\]
proposed.justification: This is now the precise root obligation: an effective all-allocation lower bridge for the corrected Airy tube, paired with the already constructed finite independent-design procedure.
proposed.gap: The exact rational spline approximation and same-input orbit calculation do not control posterior quotients uniformly over \(n^{-1/6}\) allocation perturbations, all exterior shells, and zero-count faces. Those bounds, not the old widening-density expansion, are the remaining kernel.
proposed.consumer: Once proved, the theorem will certify the sharp worst-case second-order precision of the fixed-horizon unequal three-regimen binary contrast; until then, only the fixed-design benchmark and finite same-input intervals are actionable.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove a computable diagonal \(k_n\uparrow\infty\), \(\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\downarrow0\) for the corrected Airy-tube prior whose fixed-count Bayes deficits are bounded by \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+o(1)\) uniformly on the local \(n^{-1/6}\) allocation face, every positive-count exterior shell, and every zero-count face, and combine it with a matching total finite primal construction.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen coefficient extractor only names formal arrays; it supplies no proved Taylor, Euler--Maclaurin, posterior-denominator, or quotient bound for the corrected spline density. Same-input exact enumeration gives no cross-sample modulus. In particular, neither boundary allocations nor the design optimization can be discarded, and the old polynomial family is impossible because its exact deficit diverges with \(T_n\).
open_obligations.attempted: The former widening family was stress-tested by an independent Horvitz--Thompson Bayes-risk calculation and refuted. It was replaced by compact rational spline squares converging to the Airy ground-state density while preserving the nonzero transverse response measure. The corrected prior was carried through exact positivity, finite-population target, permutation-orbit, posterior square-completion, and finite ordered-algebraic evaluation arguments. These steps do not yield the required uniform likelihood expansion.
open_obligations.partial_result: The widening-density contradiction is exact.  The replacement amplitudes \(\varphi_k^\dagger\) converge to the Airy ground state in weighted \(H^1\), have exact rational piecewise-polynomial densities, and obey the certified energy bound.  For every fixed admissible \((n,k,\varepsilon,\delta)\), the corrected prior is genuine, its all-design permutation-orbit Bayes reduction is exact, and a terminating ordered-algebraic evaluator returns a same-input risk interval.  Independently, the fixed allocation \(q^\dagger\) has second-order value \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\), and the unrestricted deficit has lower limit at least that value.

prose_updates.tldr: The advertised allocation-tube theorem is not proved and its former widening longitudinal prior is impossible: an exact Horvitz--Thompson comparison forces the scaled Bayes deficit to grow at least as \(25T/128\), so it diverges along the claimed \(T_n\to\infty\) schedule. The corrected route uses compact rational piecewise-polynomial squares converging to the Airy ground state while retaining the nonzero transverse response measure. What is proved now is the rational Airy approximation, the corrected prior's exact permutation-orbit reduction, a terminating same-input finite-risk interval, the sharp fixed-\(q^\dagger\) second-order value, and the corresponding unrestricted liminf. Uniform local, shell, and zero-face control remains the root open bridge.

project_justification.gap: The accepted parent proves the \(n^{-4/3}\) order and exact finite programs but not a common second-order limit. The former polynomial tube cannot close that gap because its longitudinal first absolute moment grows with its truncation radius. Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen and Hull remain two-arm comparators and do not supply the required unequal-three-arm all-count Bayes bridge.
project_justification.niche: For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), the eight response types, the unequal full-label score, the nonzero transverse coordinate, and \(n^{-1/6}\) allocation perturbations must be handled simultaneously. The corrected compact rational Airy family makes each finite prior exactly evaluable without allowing its first moment to diverge.
project_justification.fill: The present verified contribution is an exact obstruction to the former tube, a weighted-\(H^1\) rational Airy approximation, an exact corrected finite prior and all-design orbit reduction, a terminating same-input interval, and the fixed-design second-order benchmark. The flagship fill still requires certified uniform bounds on the corrected posterior risks over the local face, all exterior shells, and every zero-count face; no sharp unrestricted equality is claimed before that proof exists.

sampling_model.design: The causal game permits every outcome-independent assignment law, including dependence across units. For any fixed corrected permutation-invariant prior, conditioning on the realized allocation count gives the exact uniform orbit experiment and transfers its Bayes risk to arbitrary count mixtures. Uniform asymptotic optimization over all counts is not yet proved.
sampling_model.overlap: No overlap condition is imposed on the unrestricted design. Positive-count local and exterior allocations and zero-count boundary faces all remain in the corrected root obligation; none is removed by division or an interior-allocation assumption.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no superpopulation nuisances. The prior uses an exactly represented compact rational approximation to the Airy longitudinal density and keeps the explicit nonzero transverse response direction orthogonal to the finite-population contrast.

prose_updates.related_work: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, Theorem 3.1 and Appendix C) supply the two-arm scalar Airy benchmark and feedback bounds; the proved fixed-\(q^\dagger\) multiarm benchmark uses those analytic ingredients together with the response-alphabet score. Hull (2026) is also a two-arm unrestricted-design result. The accepted parent supplies first-order risk, the \(n^{-4/3}\) order, finite response-type games, and same-sample certificates, but no cross-sample all-count limit. The corrected three-arm route is therefore positioned as open at its uniform Bayes bridge, not as a completed extension of these comparators. The prospective ACTG 175 motivation concerns a prespecified complete binary-endpoint regimen contrast and is not a reanalysis of censored outcomes.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact \(K=3,n=3\) full-label gap does not determine the asymptotic design comparison. More decisively, the former widening density has \(\mathbb E|X^\dagger|=5T/16\), which yields a scaled Bayes deficit at least \(25T/128+15\varepsilon/256\) and refutes its claimed finite tube-removal limit. Compact rational Airy approximants repair that defect and support exact finite evaluation, but no proof yet bounds the corrected posterior quotients uniformly over \(n^{-1/6}\) allocation perturbations, distant positive-count shells, and zero-count faces. Consequently equality versus strict second-order loss of the independent \(q^\dagger\) design remains open.
prose_updates.honest_scope: All unconditional statements here are confined to the fixed unequal contrast \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\) and fixed \(K=3\). The fixed independent allocation has second-order value \(C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\), the unrestricted deficit has at least that lower-limit value, and every fixed rational corrected-prior input has a terminating exact-algebraic risk interval. Existence of the unrestricted limit, a matching all-procedure converse, a cross-sample threshold, and equality or strict loss of \(q^\dagger\) are not proved. No growing-\(K\), uniform vanishing-weight, arbitrary-real computability, or censored-outcome claim is made.
